sections.text:
US SOUTH REGION – MIDWEST DIVISION     ISSUED: January 1, 2026 
GENERAL MANAGER NOTICE NO. 1 
NOTICES IN EFFECT: 1 
NOTICES CANCELLED:    
TO:  ALL T&E Employees 
         RE:    Employee Expectations  
 
Road Switchers 
• Crews will report dressed and ready to commence work at start of shift 
• Engineer and brakeman will proceed directly to the locomotive(s), on board within 10 
minutes of on duty time 
o Engineer will make a full service automatic brake reduction and release to signal that 
they are on the locomotive 
o Perform inspection and air brake test (as required) 
• Conductor will contact supervisor to conduct job briefing regarding work to be completed 
within 2 minutes of on duty time 
• Crew will perform job briefing on locomotive 
• Wheels turning within 20 minutes of on duty time 
o Any impediment to these standards will be documented on the delay report and 
escalated to appropriate supervisor. 
• Meal Durations 
o 20 minute meal period 
o Movement will be commenced at expiration of meal period (30 minutes wheel stop to 
wheel start). Any issues preventing this movement will be documented on delay report 
and escalated to supervisor 
• Delay report will be kept with detailed description of any delay exceeding 5 minutes 
 
 Yard Assignments 
• Crews will report dressed and ready to commence work at start of shift 
• Engineer and helper/switchman will proceed directly to the locomotive(s), on board within 
5 minutes  
o Engineer will make a full service automatic brake reduction and release to signal they 
are on the locomotive 
o Perform inspection and air brake test (as required) 
• Conductor will contact General Yardmaster for instructions within 2 minutes of shift start for 
instructions 
• Wheels turning within 10 minutes of on duty time 
• 20 minute meal period 
o 30 minutes allowed from wheel stop to wheel start  
o Any issues that prevent movement will be escalated to Yardmaster or Manager
Road Crews 
• Crews will report dressed and ready to commence work at start of shift 
• Paperwork will be pulled or obtained (i.e. Ready packets) within 2 minutes of on duty time 
• If documents are unavailable immediately escalate to appropriate supervisor and 
document on delay report 
• Engineers of originating trains will proceed directly to the locomotive(s), on board within 10 
minutes of on duty time 
o Engineer will make a full service automatic brake reduction and release to signal that 
they are on the locomotive 
o Perform inspection and air brake test (as required) 
• Run through trains performing change off will perform a job briefing and be ready to 
proceed within 5 minutes 
• Any delay exceeding 5 minutes or situation preventing adherence to standards will be 
documented on delay report 
 
No Vacancy at Primary Hotels 
When contacting Crew Management, you must call in using the VRU 1-888-225-5127.  If unable 
to complete your task through the self-serve menu, you can select to be transferred to the crew 
dispatcher and your call will be answered in the order it is received. 
 
In the event that the primary hotel is out of rooms, crews must contact facilities at 1-877-805-8588 
to arrange alternate lodging. 
o Do not release cab until you’ve confirmed that primary hotel has rooms available, 
to avoid additional delay if needing to go to alternate hotel. 
  
If unable to get through after 10 minutes please contact CMC so that it can be escalated to the 
current manager on duty. 
 
Notifying CMC of Late Transportation  
Arrange to notify crew management if you are waiting on transportation for more than 10 
minutes past your on duty time or the required need time of your transportation.  
 
If you are on a train or need to use the radio to make the notification that you have been 
waiting for your transportation, contact the train dispatcher who will relay the information to 
crew management. 
 
Company Physical Requirements 
Employees booking off for a company physical need to schedule the appointment on a 
Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday.  CMC will need to be notified once the appointment is made. 
 
Hours of Service 
If your total time of covered service is greater than twelve (12) hours, it is your responsibility and 
expectation that you report the Hours of Service Violation to your local manager and Manager 
of Crew Management.  You may contact Sterling Joppru, CMC Manager at 612-904-5803 to 
report all HOS Violations. 
 
It is also the employee’s responsibility to report time spent at a company physical.  This can be
done by creating an Hours of Service Record in FRA Certification.  This can be done by creating 
an “OT” event.  It’s also the employee’s responsibility to be properly rested prior to and after the 
event.  If you have questions about any FRA issues, please call CMC and they will assist you.   
 
Availability Standards & 7-Day Mark Bid Preference System  
When laying off sick, T&E and Yardmaster employees must call the VRU (888-225-5127) to reach 
CMC. 
 
For CPKC to be successful and competitive in the North American Railway industry we not only 
have to provide great customer service, we have to continue our collective efforts at exceling 
on efficiency and productivity.  Given that efficiency and productivity are directly impacted by 
employee attendance levels, an attendance policy that is understood and adhered to by all is 
essential.   
  
Effective February 1, 2017 for T&E employees and January 1, 2019 for Yardmaster employees, the 
following availability standard supersedes and replaces all previous availability standards for T&E 
and Yardmaster employees at Canadian Pacific.   
 
T&E and Yardmaster employees have negotiated opportunities provided for in their Collective 
Agreements to legitimately remove themselves from the working board. Examples of negotiated 
and also legal absence categories that will not result in discipline under this availability standard 
include: annual vacation; pre-authorized personal leave; bereavement; jury duty; company 
business; and time off mandated by the hours of service regulations as amended by the Rail 
Safety Improvement Act. 
 
T&E and Yardmaster employees who book off sick or unpaid personal leave on two or more 
available work days in the calendar month will be subject to attendance review for that month. 
Disciplinary action may result. 
 
The following absence categories will be handled as more serious offenses separate from this 
calendar month review:  
 
• Miss calls (including missing calls as an ESB / demoted Engineer);  
• Booking sick or unfit on-call or after accepting a call;  
• Booking sick or unfit after call time or after start time of assignment;  
• Refusals to protect service;  
• Not reporting or reporting late for duty;  
• Unauthorized absence (AWOL);  
• Exhibiting a pattern of booking sick on weekends or consecutive to other absence types, 
such as, but not limited to: vacation, paid leave, and rest days.  
• More than 12 sick absences within one calendar year 
 
Note: Medical documentation will not be accepted to excuse these absence categories 
except in extraordinary circumstances involving a documented medical emergency. 
 
Employees requesting to have sick absences excused due to their own serious medical issues 
must ensure that satisfactory medical information is received by Health Services for review within 
three (3) business days from the last day of the medical absence. The three-business day
requirement will be strictly enforced. Upon receipt of timely and satisfactory information, the 
request will be reviewed to determine if the absence has been substantiated. Employees 
seeking leaves under FMLA or accommodations under the ADA should comply with the 
procedures in those policies.  
 
Health Services fax number is 1-800-933-8833. 
Health Services email address is CP_HealthServicesDocuments@cpkcr.com 
 
Crew Office – Methods of Contact 
• Employees being called utilizing the VRU 
o the number will show as the following 403-260-5800 (please add to contacts to avoid 
being marked as spam) 
• Employees being called directly by Crew Dispatcher 
o The number will show as the following 612-607-0150 or 612-338-5004 (please add to 
contacts to avoid being marked as spam) 
• The old direct lines that were used by many are no longer in service, all calls to the crew 
office will need to be done by calling the VRU which requires a PIN to do so (instructions 
below) 
• To declare drop turn without calling into the crew office please send email to following 
CMC0143@CPKCR.COM 
o This is for drop turns only 
• Calling in to the Shift Supervisor line for Crew Dispatcher needs will be transferred back to 
the CD line, please ensure using this number for emergencies only. 
For those employees who have not yet established permanent PIN numbers, please listen 
carefully to the prompts on the VRU. You will be asked to enter your employee number followed 
by the temporary PIN number assigned to you. Once you have entered that number, you will be 
required to establish your own personal PIN. The PIN you establish will be the one you will use for 
future calls to the VRU. 
 
In addition, please be advised of the following security considerations regarding the validation 
of PIN numbers: 
• Employee must enter a minimum PIN length – must be 4 to 7 digits. 
• Your PIN cannot be the last 4 digits of your employee number. 
• If the PIN number is 4 digits, it must contain at least four different numbers. (ie. 1212 is not a valid 
PIN number) 
 
Booking Off Investigation Requirement 
Effective immediately, employees being called by CMC for an assignment that are already 
scheduled for a formal investigation are to book off in status “I” and hold themselves out if the 
assignment the employee is being called for would impact their ability to be rested and attend 
the formal investigation.
Notifying CMC of Late Transportation 
If you are waiting on transportation for more than 10 minutes past your on-duty time or the 
required need time of your transportation, notify crew management.  
 
If you are on a train or need to use the radio to make the notification that you have been 
waiting for your transportation, contact the train dispatcher who will relay the information to 
crew management. 
 
Mechanical Assistance Coordinator (MAC) Desks 
Please contact the appropriate MAC desk: 
 
Locomotive issues 816/983-1818  
 MAC@KCSouthern.com  
 
Car-related issues 816-983-1831 
 MCD@KCSouthern.com  
 
Utilize radio communication with line-of-road trains for troubleshooting. 
 
 
Fuel Readings from Road Locomotives 
Fuel readings from all locomotives on road trains are required to be reported to the Train 
Dispatcher:  
 
• Outbound crews must report levels upon departure from a crew change location. 
• Inbound crews on arrival at the train’s final destination. 
• Whenever a train is being fueled inbound and outbound fuel levels must be reported. 
 
The only exception to this requirement is if getting fuel levels on Distributed Power will delay the 
train- If this is the case levels on Distributed Power are not required but head-end levels must still 
be reported to the Train Dispatcher. 
 
Local, RCO and Yard assignments are exempt. 
 
 
Working with Student Conductors 
While working in the field with a Student Conductor as part of your crew, it is very important for 
the Conductor to teach the student the proper way to perform different tasks of the job and 
how to remain safe while performing these tasks in the field.  
 
The Student Conductor should always be within close proximity of the Conductor on the job and 
not being used as a Brakeman or helper.  
 
Regardless of their skill level, how far along they are in their training, or previous employment, this 
is for their safety and they should also be able to demonstrate that they are able to perform the 
tasks of the job to the Conductor that is training them
Crews Must Tie Up 
It has been frequently reported and observed that numerous crew members will choose not to 
tie up and either email the crew office or leave a voicemail to have the crew office tie them up 
using the tie-up of other employee on the train. 
 
What:  As of this notice, crews are required to tie up at the conclusion of their shift. 
 
So What:  This bulletin is to conclude the practice of passing off this duty to others as it is taking 
valuable time away from other employees not responsible for the tie-up, including the Crew 
Manager and the ability to perform other critical duties of his/her job. 
 
Now What:  If not tied up prior to departing the train, download the smartphone app to do so 
remotely while in transit to the crew hotel. 
 
Away-From-Home-Terminal (AFHT) Tie Up 
When crews arrive at their Away-From-Home Terminal (AFHT) they are to tie up at that location 
as this is the location that they are off duty. Once you are tied up per Federal Regulation, the 
railroad has 30 minutes from the time you go off duty to get you to the lodging facility which is 
considered Time Off Duty. When you are called for duty at the AFHT, the time that you are called 
for is the time that you are to be at the on-duty location, not the time that you depart from the 
lodging facility. 
The following information is from the Federal Railroad Administration Hours of Service 
Compliance Manual. 
Away-From-Home-Terminal   
• FRA allows 30 minutes for commuting at the AFHT for travel between the 
release or on-duty location and lodging facility.  (OP-04-29)  
Travel to the on-duty location from lodging at the AFHT  
• One-way travel time greater than 30 minutes, including delays associated 
with transportation, will be considered as a deadhead to duty and counts as 
time on duty.    
Note:  The time a crew is delayed for personal reasons, such as stopping to buy 
items at a store or stopping to eat at a restaurant, will not count toward the 30-
minute allowance.  
Travel from the release location to lodging at the AFHT  
• One-way travel time greater than 30 minutes, including delays associated 
with transportation and lodging availability, will be considered as a 
deadhead from duty to a point of final release and counts as neither time on 
duty nor time off duty (limbo time).    
Note:  The time a crew is delayed for personal reasons, such as stopping to buy 
items at a store, or stopping to eat at a restaurant, will not count toward the 30-
minute allowance.  When an employee exceeds the 30-minute allowance 
traveling to lodging, he or she must contact Crew Management to adjust their rest.
Flashers While Operating Company Vehicles  
Effective immediately,   
The use of flashers while operating in company issued vehicles is no longer a requirement when 
driving / traversing through railway yards. The only exception to this rule change is that while 
driving / traversing in designated Intermodal Yards and Auto facilities, will still require flashers to 
use used at all times within the confines of those designated areas.    
Additional Items to note: 
• Flashers are only required in Intermodal / auto facilities when no beacon is present 
• T&E, ENG and Mech require headlights and running lights on trucks to be used (al languages 
are worded the same) while operating in rail yards. 
• T&E, MECH and ENG wi8ll continue to require ATV/UTV to use lights and beacons if equipped. 
• ENG requires head and taillights as well as beacon when on track and operating under 
GCOR/OTS Rules. 
 
 
Train Procedures for 968-Type Trains with Shreveport Origin  
 
 
Purpose: 
 
To ensure safe handling of intermodal traffic and prevent service delays caused by open doors or damaged lading. 
 
Effective Immediately: 
 
Due to a recent rise in online service interruptions caused by open intermodal container doors and exposed lading on the 
Speedway Subdivision, the following procedures will apply to all 968-type trains originating out of Union Pacific’s 
Hollywood Yard. 
 
Crew On-Duty and Dress-in-Ready: 
 
Crews reporting for duty at Shreveport will adhere to GM Midwest Dress-in-Ready standards and proceed directly to their 
train after completing all required paperwork. Crews must maintain their mode of transportation for immediate deployment. 
 
•    Roll-By Inspection: 
The conductor will perform a roll-by inspection while the train departs Hollywood Yard, observing for any open 
intermodal container doors, vandalism, or product/lading protruding from cars. 
 
•    Reporting and Coordination: 
If any open doors or product damage are observed, the conductor must immediately notify the train dispatcher and 
await dispatcher instructions before proceeding. 
 
Once the roll-by is completed and no issues are observed, the conductor will coordinate with the locomotive engineer 
and dispatcher to be brought to the nearest road crossing to expedite eastward train movement.
Gravity Dropping Prohibited on Midwest Division and Shreveport Yard 
Effective immediately, crews are prohibited from gravity dropping cars on the Midwest 
Division and 
Shreveport Yard. 
 
Trains Requiring Signals at West Wye – Kansas City 
Effective immediately, any train waiting longer than five (5) minutes for a signal at West Wye in 
Kansas City must contact the Knoche Yardmaster and advise that they are unable to obtain a 
signal at West Wye. 
 
This notification is required to ensure awareness and coordination when delays are 
encountered at West Wye.  
 
 
 
We will all go Home Safe; Working Safely Together.  
 
 
Work smart, stay safe. 
  
Brandon Billingsley 
General Manager 
U.S. Midwest

SOUTH REGION - MIDWEST DIVISION ISSUED:  January 1, 2026 
GENERAL MANAGER NOTICE NO. 4 
 
NOTICES IN EFFECT: 1-4 
NOTICES CANCELLED:  
 
TO: ALL T&E Employees  
RE: Trains 180 and 181 
 
 
All 180/181 train symbols are to isolate locomotives as follows: 
• Only one locomotive can be online per 3640 tons. 
• Trains over 3640 tons may have two locomotives online. 
Additional locomotives in the head end consist are to be isolated first. If additional locomotives 
are present, idle the tail end remote first, then mid-train remote(s) as applicable. 
To prevent a stall on a Heavy or Mountain grade, one additional locomotive may be placed 
online. When placing a locomotive back online, select a remote locomotive first (where 
applicable). Such locomotive must be isolated immediately once the movement has 
ascended the grade. 
In FTO operation: 
• Trains required to ISOLATE trailing units must continue to run using FTO. 
• Trains required to IDLE 
remotes shall also run 
FTO by taking 
advantage of a new 
FTO feature that 
allows the last remote 
to be idled while in FTO. This new button is in the FTO “Restrictions” page. 
 
If this button is not available, trains required to IDLE their remote must run manual.

sections.title: GM #6 — Tips & Tricks for iPads — January 1, 2026
sections.text:
US SOUTH REGION - MIDWEST DIVISION ISSUED: January 1, 2026  
GENERAL MANAGER NOTICE NO. 6  
  
NOTICES IN EFFECT: 1-6  
NOTICES CANCELLED:  
TO:   ALL T&E Employees   
RE:  Tips & Tricks for iPads  
 
 
Employees must report for duty with iPad. 
Device must be charged and available for use for the duration of shift. 
Employees are required to report all work via iPad. 
Notify trainmaster of exceptions when arriving for duty. 
 
If you are experiencing issues with your iPads, check to make sure you are not in training mode:  
1. Switch & Build (see Job Aid on Page 3 of this bulletin): 
a. Tap on Change Station 
b. Tap on Exit Training Mode 
c. Double tap the home button and swipe the apps off the screen 
d. Open Switch & Build and select your Region, Major Terminal & Station (ID) 
e. Go to Comp Portal app and tap on devices 
f. Select your device and tap Check Status 
2. AIR 2.0 (see Job Aid on Page 4 of this bulletin): 
a. Tap on the Release Train button 
b. Double tap the home button and swipe the apps off the screen 
c. Open AIR 2.0 and select your Region and Origin Station

Due to multiple recent incidents that cars are being pulled from customer facilities that are not billed, 
CPKC Employees are to refresh themselves with the Required Documentation section of the CPKC 
USHMIR outlined below for your convenience of reference.  
 
SECTION II.  REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION 
 
1. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 
It is not acceptable to pick up a hazmat car at a customer location with only a shipper-
supplied shipping document.  Only lift/pull cars requiring a dangerous goods document from a 
shipper siding if a CPKC compressed waybill is available or, the cars are listed to lift/pull on the 
work order or identified as late work instructions received through electronic means 
(FIT/Printer/AIR/FAX).  
No person may accept a hazardous material for shipment by rail transportation or transport a 
hazardous material in a train unless a member of the crew has each of the following: 
a. acceptable shipping documents 
b. acceptable emergency response information 
c. a document showing the current position of the hazardous material shipment in the train. 
Notes: 
1) Electronic Documents are only acceptable with Railroads having authorization from DOT. Paper 
or Electronic documents (shipper supplied or (FIT/Printer/AIR/FAX) generated compressed waybill) 
are still required documentation when moving hazardous materials rail cars. 
2) The purpose of this documentation is to provide railroad personnel and emergency response 
personnel with accurate information about the hazardous materials.
Therefore, keep all current hazardous material documents neat and orderly and ensure that they are 
available in case of an emergency or for inspection. Properly discard superseded documents to 
eliminate the possibility of confusing or inconsistent information. 
 
Exceptions: 
1) Hazardous Materials rail cars that are released empty and no longer meet the definition of a 
regulated car may be lifted/pulled. (i.e. not a residue last contained rail car). 
2) Hazardous Materials cars received at interchange. 
3) Intermodal shipments are excluded.

At CPKC we prioritize the use of Trip Optimizer and Talos as fuel savings technologies. However, 
maximizing fuel efficiency also relies on the expertise and real-time decision-making of our engineers and 
dispatchers when running trains without the technology. This is the purpose of the Hypermilers program. 
  
To support this effort, we are excited to announce the upcoming launch of the Hypermilers Program. This 
initiative is designed to educate engineers on fuel conservation principles and recognize and reward 
those who leverage their knowledge of territory-specific conditions to uncover fuel-saving opportunities 
as they arise. 
  
In the meantime, for trains not equipped with energy management systems, please refer to the following 
coaching instructions to help conserve fuel. 
 
Southbound 
 
Approaching speed change at Goodman (Starting at mile 181) 
- Use throttle modulation and low DB to slow down for speed change 
- Avoid airbrake and excessive DB where possible 
 
Tipping downhill at Westville (Starting at mile 242) 
- Throttle down earlier to maintain a target speed of 25 mph 
- Do not exceed target speed while in throttle. 
- Use the hill to accelerate the train to track speed. (Once transitioned to idle or DB)  
 
Tipping downhill at mile 260 (Starting at mile 258) 
- Throttle down earlier to reduce to a target speed of 25 mph 
- Do not exceed target speed while in throttle. 
- Use the hill to accelerate the train to track speed. (Once transitioned to idle or DB)  
 
Approaching Sallisaw (Starting at mile 287) 
- Use throttle modulation to slow down for interlocker. 
- Avoid short bursts of speed. 
 
Tipping downhill coming into Gains (Starting at mile 297) 
- Throttle down earlier to maintain to a target speed of 30 mph 
- Do not exceed target speed while in throttle. 
- Use the hill to accelerate the train to track speed. (Once transitioned to idle or DB)  
 
Approaching speed change at Howe (Starting at mile 329) 
- Use throttle modulation to slow down for speed change 
- Avoid airbrake and excessive DB where possible
Northbound 
 
Tipping downhill at mile 242 (Starting at mile 244) 
- Throttle down earlier to reduce a target speed of 25 mph 
- Do not exceed target speed while in throttle. 
- Use the hill to accelerate the train to track speed. (Once transitioned to idle or DB)  
 
Tipping downhill at Decatur (Starting at mile 220) 
- Throttle down earlier to reduce a target speed of 20 mph 
- Do not exceed target speed while in throttle. 
- Use the hill to accelerate the train to track speed. (Once transitioned to idle or DB)

SUBJECT: FAMTRIP (Familiarization) Expectations and Training Plan Requirements 
 
Effective immediately, all employees assigned to familiarization (FAMTRIP), whether 
conductor or engineer, must contact their assigned Road Foreman of Engines within 24 hours 
of bid issuance. 
 
The purpose of this contact is to establish a training plan, which will include designated off 
days and the sequence of trips required to achieve full qualification. 
    •    Employees headquartered in Shreveport will observe Monday as their scheduled off 
day following 
    the change of the mark. 
    •    Employees headquartered in Kansas City will observe Saturday as their scheduled off 
day. 
 
Training plans will be built around current qualifications and remaining territory requirements 
in all directions out of the home terminal. Each plan will include specific train numbers to be 
taken. 
 
Any deviation from the approved plan—including falling short of a location or being taxied 
in—must be immediately escalated to the assigned Road Foreman to establish a follow-up 
training trip. For example, if an employee falls short of a location such as Heavener while 
traveling north and is taxied in, they must notify the Road Foreman. Once rested, that 
employee will be dispatched to complete the remaining leg of the journey and will double-
pillow in that location to ensure full qualification. 
 
Employees familiarizing out of Shreveport or Heavener are to contact Road Foreman 
Christopher Irving or Bobby Rivers. 
Employees familiarizing out of Kansas City are to contact Road Foreman Matthew Rimmer. 
 
Once employees traverse over the territory, they are required to take the familiarization 
exam. Upon qualification, it is the employee’s responsibility to maintain all active territorial 
qualifications. In the event that a qualification is approaching expiration, the employee must 
notify their appropriate supervisor no less than 60 days prior and make arrangements to

Class Coding: For joint industry customers, railcars previously class coded with a JIND or JI

inventory.

• Railcars placed at joint industries will remain visible in CPKC systems. 
• Customer can now use the Customer Station portal to request supplemental activities 
such as intra-plant switching at these locations.

Another/Same Track” or “Move for Switch” can now be directly reported using the AIR

or working as conductor or engineer trainees.

any reason, an employee cannot be in the lead locomotive due to a seat issue or any other

controlling and operating the train. Familiarization is not a ride-along. If an engineer is unable to 
operate the train for any reason, this must be escalated immediately to the appropriate supervisor on 
duty. 
 
Upon returning from a familiarization trip, employees are required to report to the appropriate 
supervisor or supervisor on duty and complete their territory examination. Once the examination is 
completed, the employee will be listed as qualified on the territory.

SUBJECT: Vehicle Operations  
 
 
Pre-Trip Vehicle Requirements 
Before operating a vehicle for company business, drivers must: 
1. Conduct a 360-degree walk-around inspection to identify hazards, obstructions, or unsafe conditions. 
2. Complete all required daily vehicle inspection reports prior to use. 
3. Immediately report unsafe conditions, defects, or damage to a supervisor. 
4. Remove defective vehicles from service until repaired or properly tagged. 
 
2. General Operating Requirements 
1. Drivers are fully accountable for the safe and controlled operation of the vehicle. 
2. Passengers are required to verbally alert the driver if unsafe conditions or behaviors are observed. 
3. Seat belts must be worn by all occupants at all times when equipped. 
4. Headlights or daytime running lights must be on while the vehicle is in operation. 
5. Vehicles must not be operated with doors open or while entering/exiting a moving vehicle. 
6. All tools, materials, and equipment must be properly secured. This includes laptops.  
 
3. Mobile Device Use 
1. Company-issued cell phones may be used hands-free only and solely for company business when: 
o It is safe to do so, and 
o Such use is permitted by applicable state, provincial, or local laws. 
2. Personal cell phones are prohibited while operating company vehicles unless: 
o Explicit authorization is granted, and 
o A company phone has not been provided. 
 
 
4. Parking & Reversing Safety 
1. Pull-through parking must be used when available. 
2. When pull-through parking is unavailable, vehicles should be backed into parking spaces unless unsafe. 
3. Vehicles may not be parked within six (6) feet of railroad tracks unless proper protection is in place. 
4. Unattended vehicles must be: 
o Secured against movement (park, brake set, chocks if required) 
o Turned off with keys removed 
o Locked with all compartments and windows closed 
 
 
Failure to comply with this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including loss of driving privileges, 
corrective action, or termination.

TO: All T&E Employees 
SUBJECT: Instructions for Deadhead Crews     
 
Effective immediately, all deadhead crews arriving into Kansas City, St. Louis, Pittsburgh, Heavener, and 
Shreveport must contact the on-duty Trainmaster by phone and receive verbal permission to tie up prior 
to booking off. 
 
If the on-duty Trainmaster cannot be reached, crews will continue attempting contact every five minutes 
and must also attempt to contact the Corridor Manager. Crews will not tie up until contact is made. If 
contact has not been established by the 10th hour on duty, crews may tie up and go home. 
 
Deadhead crews arriving at any other location must contact the Corridor Manager by phone and 
receive verbal permission prior to booking off. 
 
In addition, any crew at an away-from-home terminal in Kansas City must contact the Tower Trainmaster 
by phone prior to initiating their deadhead home. 
 
Documentation of all call attempts, including times and the name of the individual granting verbal 
permission, must be recorded on the crew’s trip delay report and submitted at the end of the tour of 
duty. 
 
 
 
We will all go Home Safe; Working Safely Together.  
 
 
Work smart, stay safe.

following instructions:

depart Hollywood yard. After receiving clearance, reach out to the UPRR Lufkin Subdivision 
dispatcher 418 on radio channel 96-96 *18 for a signal at CP RB230.

• Releasing handbrakes from the ground when the wheel is above shoulder height  
Switch handling and on or about tracks are showing up every month. Check your points before and after

US SOUTH REGION – MIDWEST DIVISION    ISSUED: April 15, 2026   
GENERAL MANAGER NOTICE NO. 31 
NOTICES IN EFFECT: 1-31 
NOTICES CANCELLED:    
TO: All T&E Employees  
SUBJECT: EEBA Inspection and Training  
 
MANDATORY EEBA INSPECTION BEFORE EVERY TOUR OF DUTY 
All US crew members must inspect their assigned Emergency Escape Breathing Apparatus (EEBA) using the iPad EEBA 
Inspection App or FIT Kiosk before starting any tour of duty.  
Unless otherwise instructed, EEBA use is required when performing train service of any type. This includes yard assignments, 
deadhead service, and taxi travel.  
In Canada and Mexico, crews are only required to inspect and carry an EEBA when originating-from or destined-to a Canada–
US or Mexico–US border location, including when deadheading. Follow local instructions for EEBA use. 
 
HOW TO INSPECT YOUR EEBA 
• Open the EEBA App on your iPad or use a FIT Kiosk. 
• Log in using your CPKC User ID (do not use a KCS User ID). 
o Inspections must be completed using your own login and the device you are personally using. 
• Scan your assigned EEBA or enter the serial number. 
o Do not scan or record inspections on behalf of another employee. 
• Perform the inspection. 
o Each crew member must inspect and scan their own assigned EEBA. 
• Record the result (Pass/Fail) in the app. 
 
In Canada and Mexico, crews must inspect the EEBA issued to them, including units signed out from lockers. 
  
IF THE APP OR DEVICE IS UNAVAILABLE 
Use the EEBA Manual Inspection Form (paper log) available at your terminal. 
• Fill out all required fields. 
• Submit the completed form before departure. 
• Notify your local manager. 
  
FAILED INSPECTION? 
Do NOT proceed with a failed EEBA. 
Immediately notify your local manager and get a replacement and/or follow further instructions. 
  
TRAINING & SUPPORT 
The following EEBA training is mandatory: 
• Course 3940.4 – EEBA for US Train Crews – Online 
• Course 3940.5 – EEBA for US Train Crews – French Online 
• Course 3440.6 – EEBA for US Train Crews – Spanish Online 
 
Job aids and inspection manuals are available on CPKC SharePoint under “Operations Training Materials” 
 
For assistance, contact your supervisor. For technical assistance, contact the Help Desk.

Work smart, stay safe.
